Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: The original claim that no off-grid policy exists is not supported by the evidence. Eritrea's Energy Policy (2009, reaffirmed with a 20%-renewables-by-2030 target) explicitly provides for rural electrification and off-grid solar, backed by real deployment: EU/UNDP-funded solar hybrid mini-grids at Areza and Maidma (commissioned 2018, ~40,000 beneficiaries) and an AfDB-funded USD19.5m, 12MW 'Desert to Power' mini-grid programme (agreement signed March 2025) for Teseney, Kerekebet and Barentu targeting roughly 235,000 people. Recalculated to 3 (Active policy with some deployment) — implemented via the Ministry of Energy and Mines/Eritrea Electricity Corporation, though still substantially donor-financed rather than a mature, comprehensive domestic programme.
